ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner must be screened before onboarding against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) guidance, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC's SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists, the United Kingdom Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Amendment) Regulations, and the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020 lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for domestic or foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including their immediate family members and close associates; any PEP trigger must be escalated to the compliance officer for senior management approval before account activation. Ongoing monitoring includes adverse media, name matching against daily sanctions updates, and annual re-screening. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years in accordance with record-keeping obligations under the AML/CFT Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Online Company Name Reservation and Search Portal (companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement that company names consist of Latin alphabet characters only (A-Z), plus permitted punctuation, spaces, and numerics; non-Latin scripts (including Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, and devanagari) are rejected. Phonetic transliteration into English or Māori is mandatory for any foreign-language name. The four-tier naming convention comprises: (1) the distinctive coined or patronymic element; (2) the legal term 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (or 'Tapui' for Māori'); (3) an optional business descriptor; and (4) no reference to the company number. A name must not be identical or 'so nearly similar as to be likely to deceive' to an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar of Companies rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written appeal through the Companies Office portal within 20 working days, stating the proposed name, the rejection grounds, and evidence of non-confusion (e.g., trademark registrations, common law use, or contextual distinctiveness). The Registrar will issue a determination within 10 working days; if rejected again, the applicant may apply for an administrative review by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment. As a final step, judicial review may be sought in the High Court under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972. All appeal submissions must be retained in the due diligence file.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office with a physical New Zealand street address (not a PO Box) is accepted by the Companies Office for registration purposes, but Inland Revenue and New Zealand banks generally reject a pure virtual mailbox or commercial mail holding provider when establishing GST registration and a business bank account, particularly for an ISIC 6201 SaaS company receiving ACH payments. The entity must demonstrate commercial substance through a local resident director, physical records accessible in New Zealand, and a genuine operational presence such as a serviced office or co-working agreement with a specific suite number. A mailbox-only arrangement will likely fail tax and banking due diligence and may trigger anti-avoidance review under the Income Tax Act 2007. Therefore, for this PropTech entity, a physical serviced office lease or hybrid workspace is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) company-name signage or digital display at registered premises; (2) staff or director present during business hours; (3) availability of physical share register, board minutes, and accounting records; (4) valid occupancy agreement matching the registered address; (5) evidence of local IT infrastructure or procurement. For unregulated PropTech SaaS with low AML risk, the quantified probability of an unannounced physical inspection by municipal authorities or the Registrar within the first 12 months is approximately 10-15%. This risk rises to 30% or more if the company claims R&D refunds, incurs persistent tax losses, or engages in high-volume related-party cross-border payments. Municipal tax teams may verify commercial substance through site visits after GST registration, and failure to pass an inspection can result in compulsory deregistration and penalty warnings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), Part 2 ss 10-25, Part 4 ss 41-87, Part 7 ss 120-126, and Part 8 ss 151-191; Constitution of the Company (as adopted)

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 - Application for Registration of a Company under the Companies Act 1993 filed electronically via the New Zealand Companies Office online registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law does not impose any minimum paid-up capital requirement. Shares may be issued for cash, services, or other consideration as determined by the directors. There is no blocked escrow account requirement; the Company may issue shares at par as recorded in the share register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability and Corporate Structure Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Business Names and Companies Register online portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing incorporation, the applicant must search the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name and does not contravene the name restrictions in the Companies Act 1993. If a particular trading name is desired, use the online name reservation function to secure it for up to twenty working days. The applicant must also determine whether the Company will adopt the default constitution or file a tailored constitution, and confirm the registered office address is a physical New Zealand address capable of receiving legal service. All proposed directors and shareholders must provide consent and identification. The structure should be documented with a simple capitalization table and beneficial ownership statement before the formal application is submitted.
required_dossiers: Completed company name reservation application (if name reservation is desired)
Proposed constitution of the Company or confirmation that the Companies Act 1993 default provisions will apply
Consent to act as director forms for each proposed director
Consent to act as shareholder forms for each initial shareholder
Passport or national identity documents for all directors and shareholders
Registered office address proof and landlord or building owner consent to service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, conduct an additional register search using a distinctive alphanumeric or geographic qualifier, obtain a letter of consent from the holder of a similar name, or submit a formal reconsideration request to the Companies Office. If the constitution raises questions, submit a revised constitution and seek a compliance review before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Application for Incorporation and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) via the online filing service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online statutory application for incorporation using the exact legal name approved or reserved, the physical registered office address, the address for service, the full names and birthdates of directors, the names of shareholders, share classes, number of shares, and any constitution or agreed exclusion of default provisions. The applicant must certify that the Company will operate lawfully, that every director has consented to act, and that the registered office is available. Payment of the prescribed government filing fee is made by credit card or online payment at submission. Once the Registrar is satisfied, the Company is immediately registered and a certificate of incorporation is issued electronically. The Company exists from the date of registration and cannot act before that date.
required_dossiers: Form 2 electronic application for company registration
Consent to act as director for each director
Consent of each registered office provider or address owner
Initial shareholders subscription and share allotment schedule
Constitution, if adopted
Government-issued photo identification for each director and shareholder
Valid RealMe account credentials and contact email
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the indicated fields and resubmit within the Companies Office response window. If the application is suspended due to identity or consent issues, file fresh affidavits or identity declarations, add a resolving notation to the dossier, and re-present the corrected e-form. If refusal is based on a statutory name or regulatory ground, the applicant may file a reconsideration request and, if necessary, seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Inland Revenue, Activate NZBN, and Complete Tax Status Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand; New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Registry operated by MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receiving the certificate of incorporation, the Company should automatically receive a New Zealand Business Number, which should be verified in the Companies Register. The Company must apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number; directors and beneficial owners with New Zealand tax obligations must confirm their IRD numbers. The Company must assess whether taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, requiring compulsory goods and services tax registration. If the Company will have employees, it must register for PAYE and other employer obligations. The company should also confirm whether it is a non-resident foreign company for tax classification and whether any withholding tax obligations apply to dividends or services. All tax registration fields should match the Companies Office record exactly to avoid mismatched filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation from the Companies Office
New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) confirmation
IRD number application or confirmation for directors and beneficial owners
Projected revenue and GST registration assessment
Director and shareholder residential address information
Company constitution and share register extract
Bank account details for IRD refunds and payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD registration is rejected or delayed, contact the IRD business integrity team, provide certified copies of the certificate of incorporation and identifications, and file a paper IRD registration form with a covering declaration. If a GST registration application is queried, correct the estimated turnover figure and provide a detailed revenue forecast to demonstrate the expected threshold.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account, Complete AML/CFT Onboarding, and Effect Banking Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised New Zealand registered bank or non-bank lending institution; Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT supervisor if the Company becomes a financial service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The authorized directors and signatories must attend a corporate bank onboarding meeting or complete the bank's electronic onboarding portal. The bank will require certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitution, first board resolution, banking mandate, and identification for every director and beneficial owner. The Company must complete anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism customer due diligence, providing a transparent ownership structure, nature of business statement, source of funds, anticipated transaction volumes, and target payment rails including Stripe Billing and ACH Direct. Because the business is a low-risk PropTech real-estate SaaS platform, the bank will ordinarily apply standard rather than enhanced due diligence. After final execution of the banking mandate, corporate debit cards, online banking tokens, and payment gateway integrations may be activated.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Constitution and first board resolution including banking mandate
Passport or national ID of each authorized signatory and beneficial owner
Proof of registered office and address for service
Business plan describing the ISIC 6201 software services
Source of wealth and source of funds declaration
AML/CFT beneficial ownership chart
NZBN certificate and IRD registration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide a clear trust and corporate ownership chart, audited or accountant-certified financial evidence, and a statutory declaration of lawful source of funds. If the application is declined, apply to another registered New Zealand bank with a simplified ownership structure and physical presence, and provide additional references to support the low-risk classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - No industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over a pure digital PropTech SaaS entity under ISIC 6201; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations under ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx are conducted.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - No industrial or manufacturing operating license is required for a software-as-a-service property management and rental screening cloud platform; the activity does not involve physical goods production, chemical conversion, assembly, or warehousing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - No environmental regulatory agency filing is required for zero-emission digital software operations; the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) is referenced for completeness but holds no permitting jurisdiction over this SaaS activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - No wastewater discharge points, volatile organic compound emission sources, or hazardous waste handling activities exist in server-based software operations. The Company's IT infrastructure is powered by commercial data-center electricity contracts and does not trigger environmental discharge licensing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - No Civil Defense fire permit or structural load inspection is required because the Company occupies ordinary office premises rather than an industrial site. Standard occupational safety and health obligations under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 nevertheless require a compliant workplace risk assessment for office-based staff and a health and safety policy proportionate to the low-risk digital consulting environment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand; online portal: myIR Secure Online Services via www.ird.govt.nz. For export physical clearance, the competent authority is the New Zealand Customs Service (NZCS), operating the Trade Single Window (TSW) for electronic customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity, the statutory tax identifier is the New Zealand IRD number, which also serves as the GST registration number; there is no separate VAT/GST ID. The standard procurement procedure is: (1) determine whether the non-resident entity has a New Zealand tax obligation, such as carrying on a taxable activity, making supplies to New Zealand consumers exceeding the GST registration threshold, deriving New Zealand-sourced income, or being required to withhold New Zealand tax; (2) complete the Inland Revenue Department non-individual IRD number application, denoted in Inland Revenue practice as form IR596, for a company or other non-individual entity; (3) provide certified copies of the entity constitution, certificate of incorporation, directors and shareholders register, registered office address, tax residence jurisdiction, and, where the document is not in English, a certified English translation; (4) where the foreign entity has a fixed place of business or continuous business activity in New Zealand, first register the foreign company with the New Zealand Companies Office and appoint a resident New Zealand agent for service of tax documents and notices, as required by New Zealand tax administration practice; (5) submit the application and supporting documentation through myIR or, for non-resident entities without myIR access, through the prescribed Inland Revenue paper application channel; and (6) retain the IRD number confirmation in the entity's permanent tax file. The same IRD number is used for income tax, GST, withholding tax, and other New Zealand indirect tax obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A New Zealand limited liability company is a separate tax-paying entity subject to company income tax on a residency basis; a New Zealand incorporated company is resident and taxed on worldwide income, while a foreign-incorporated non-resident company is taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income unless its management is effectively in New Zealand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box election. Qualifying closely held New Zealand companies may elect look-through company (LTC) treatment under the Income Tax Act 2007, subject to strict shareholder and eligibility conditions. There is no elective hybrid mismatch mechanism; OECD/great hybrid mismatch and anti-avoidance rules apply mandatorily where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period for taxable supplies connected with New Zealand; a non-resident supplier of remote services or digital services, including software-as-a-service platforms, is required to register for GST when the value of supplies to New Zealand residents exceeds NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, with voluntary registration available below that threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. New Zealand has no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory e-invoicing API validation, no anti-fraud digital stamping, and no government pre-clearance of invoices. Invoices must contain the standard GST tax invoice particulars prescribed by the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and be retained for audit. Electronic invoicing is permitted, and the voluntary PEPPOL-based New Zealand e-Invoicing network may be used; GST returns and payments are filed through the Inland Revenue myIR portal, without an API clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods qualifies for 0% GST when the goods are exported from New Zealand by the supplier and the export is evidenced by the New Zealand Customs export declaration and transport documentation. A supply of services, including SaaS/PropTech platform access, qualifies for 0% GST under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the service is supplied to a person who is non-resident and outside New Zealand at the time the service is performed, and the service is not directly connected with New Zealand land, New Zealand moveable property, or a natural resource. The SaaS subscriber must be a non-resident with no New Zealand place of business using the platform for New Zealand domestic enjoyment. The supplier must obtain and retain contemporaneous commercial evidence of the recipient's non-resident status, foreign business address, offshore use, and foreign payment. GST-registered zero-rated exporters may also claim input credits and receive refunds from Inland Revenue for GST incurred on business inputs attributable to those zero-rated export supplies, subject to the same documentary substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs export declaration (Export Entry) lodged electronically through the Trade Single Window, showing exporter IRD number, goods description, value, and overseas destination
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight evidencing physical export from New Zealand to the foreign consignee
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the exported goods or services and the overseas buyer
Signed SaaS platform subscription agreement, contract, or order form identifying the non-resident customer, their foreign tax/business address, and the place of use
GST tax invoice issued by the supplier quoting the supplier IRD/GST number and stating that the supply is zero-rated for export under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985

Foreign exchange payment/remittance evidence such as a SWIFT MT103, foreign currency bank account statement, or bank credit advice; New Zealand does not issue an Inward Remittance Certificate, and the latter is not a New Zealand statutory requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where a zero-rated export supply is not supported by the required documentation, Inland Revenue may redetermine the supply as standard-rated, assess GST at 15%, disallow associated input tax credits, and impose use-of-money interest from the due date of the GST return. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, shortfall penalties may apply at 20% for unacceptable tax positions, 40% for abusive tax positions, and 150% for evasion or fraudulent intent, with separate penalties for failing to take reasonable care or failing to keep sufficient records. Knowingly filing a false GST return or knowingly evading GST can lead to criminal liability under the Tax Administration Act 1994, including fines and imprisonment, and false Customs declarations may be prosecuted under the Customs and Excise Act 2018. Records supporting export zero-rating must be retained for seven years. The general reassessment time bar is four years from the date the return was filed, but no time limit applies where the shortfall arises from evasion, fraud, or insufficient disclosure, meaning retrospective clawback can occur many years after the original zero-rating position.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates under a fully liberalised and free-floating exchange rate regime. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not administer exchange controls or restrict the convertibility of the New Zealand dollar for current account or capital account transactions. The country has accepted Article VIII obligations of the International Monetary Fund, meaning there are no restrictions on payments and transfers for current international transactions, and no discriminatory currency practices. Capital inflows and outflows are freely permitted, subject only to general anti-money laundering obligations and, in limited circumstances, overseas investment screening for significant acquisitions of sensitive land or fishing quota, none of which applies to a software-as-a-service real estate technology entity. Profit remittance by foreign shareholders is not subject to FX approval or mandatory conversion requirements, provided corporate tax obligations are satisfied and standard bank compliance requests are met. Dividend distributions may be remitted in NZD or any freely accepted foreign currency through normal banking channels. There are no surrender requirements on export proceeds, and no requirement to repatriate overseas earnings. The practical compliance burden is limited to accurate purpose codes for balance of payments statistics and robust documentary trails for bank due diligence. Overall, New Zealand presents no structural obstacle for cross-border treasury operations, and the currency is fully convertible on a spot and forward basis within the domestic interbank market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand imposes no statutory surrender requirements and no mandatory conversion timelines for export foreign currency receipts. Exporters may retain foreign currency earnings indefinitely in external or domestic accounts and are free to convert to NZD at commercial exchange rates. The only reporting obligations are statistical data collection by the Reserve Bank and suspicious transaction reporting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) operating in New Zealand must be enrolled as reporting entities under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. They are legally permitted to offer payment and e-money services, but they cannot accept deposits or conduct banking business without a registered bank licence under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. For a PropTech real estate SaaS platform, offshore digital EMIs such as Airwallex, Stripe, or Wise can be viable for payment routing, client refunds, and low-value disbursements, but they should not be used as the primary treasury clearing house for statutory capital injections or high-value trade settlements. Domestic Tier-1 banks provide more reliable access to the New Zealand payment system, the Real-Time Gross Settlement infrastructure, and SWIFT connectivity for both NZD and foreign currency. EMIs are further constrained by their licensing jurisdictions and by New Zealand bank concentration arrangements, so treasury strategy should hold Tier-1 bank accounts as the principal operational backbone and use EMIs selectively for inbound SaaS subscription collections and outbound recurring refunds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand statutory directors are not required to appear physically in-branch for corporate account opening if the bank can complete customer due diligence through reliable independent verification. Remote video interviews are generally accepted as part of a risk-based approach, supported by certified copies of best evidence, a board resolution authorising signatories, and a completed know-your-customer package. Consular proxy opening is not a standard recognised method; New Zealand banks typically require the company's authorised signatories or professional introducers to complete verification. For non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners, banks may mandate a recorded video conference to confirm identity, source of wealth, and intended business activities. A physical presence mandate can be waived where the account is for a New Zealand registered company with clear corporate documentation, commercial substance, and no adverse sanctions or money-laundering risk indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder injecting capital from multiple jurisdictions with opaque source-of-wealth evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified corporate registry extract of the ultimate parent, a 12-month original bank statement chain in the remitting entity's name, formal source-of-wealth statement signed by the beneficial owner, income tax assessment or certificate of tax residence for the funding entities, a board resolution approving the capital injection, a legal opinion confirming no adverse regulatory finding, and a sworn declaration of no third-party financing or hidden principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership chain involving trusts or nominee shareholders obscuring true controllers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit an illustrated ownership and control chart, full trust deed or equivalent constitutional documents, a registered agent confirmation of the settlor, trustee, and protector identities, certificate of incorporation and good standing for every intermediate entity, results of a desktop due diligence search on each control level, and a professional legal opinion that the economic substance of the structure is not designed to evade transparency obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PropTech platform receiving rental and property management funds, creating third-party payment and client-money exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited financial statements or a client-funds trust account certificate, a payment flow diagram distinguishing platform operating revenues from client rental monies, signed service agreements with property owners and tenants, AML/CFT compliance programme documentation, annual independent assurance report, data protection policies, and contractual clauses confirming that client funds are safeguarded and not available to creditors of the company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Director or ultimate beneficial owner flagged by sanctions or PEP screening with insufficient corroborating identity evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver original or certified passport and national identity documents, proof of residential address, evidence of citizenship or permanent residence, an independent sanctions and adverse-media screening report, an explanation memorandum for any politically exposed person status, regulatory clearances or court records where applicable, and a legal opinion from a qualified practitioner confirming that no Proceeds of Crime Act or Terrorism Suppression Act risk materialises from onboarding.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital is routed as a SWIFT MT103 credit to the New Zealand company's capital escrow account. The remitting institution should state purpose code CAP or a code accepted by the receipient bank under the Balance of Payment statistical framework, with narrative such as 'Share Subscription' or 'Equity Contribution'. New Zealand does not require FX approval, but the receiving bank will require a board resolution approving the share issuance, a signed share subscription agreement, a completed AML/CFT source-of-funds questionnaire, and evidence of the beneficial owner identity. Capital verification is performed by the company's directors and auditors through the New Zealand Companies Office registry, updating the share register and issuing share certificates. No statutory minimum capital is required for this entity, although the injection should be economically coherent. Foreign currency inward remittances may be settled into NZD via the bank's spot rate or held in a foreign currency account depending on treasury policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operating disbursements are cleared through SWIFT MT103 payments for bank-to-bank transfers, commercial letters of credit for documentary purchase arrangements, and documentary collections where bank obligation ease is not required. For recurring SaaS subscription refunds, the company may use Stripe Billing and ACH Direct rails within the United States, while New Zealand domestic suppliers are paid through local NZD clearing in the Real-Time Gross Settlement system. Cross-border supplier payments for software infrastructure, cloud hosting, marketing services, and real estate data licences should be routed directly from the Tier-1 New Zealand bank account with clear invoices and contract references to satisfy AML/CFT audit trails. For high-value agricultural or property-related purchases, a confirmed irrevocable letter of credit issued by the New Zealand bank and advised by a corresponding foreign bank provides settlement security. All trade disbursements must align with the documented business purpose of the PropTech platform and must not involve tax evasion, terrorism financing, or sanctioned counterparties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards quoted by New Zealand licensed banks for NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD, and other freely traded currency pairs
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be used only for currencies with legal restrictions, but not for NZD because the New Zealand dollar is fully deliverable in the spot and forward markets
Cross-currency swaps arranged through the corporate banking relationship to manage long-term foreign currency funding and interest rate risk
Plain-vanilla currency options and rolling FX swaps offered under the bank's standard ISDA documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the New Zealand Companies Office (online annual confirmation of company details)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the filing window opens 28 days before the annual-return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers an overdue-company status; the Registrar may issue a final notice and, if the return remains unfiled, commence administrative strike-off under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993 (typically after annual returns are more than two years overdue), after publication of a Gazette removal notice allowing at least 20 working days to object. The company and every director commit an offence and may be fined up to NZD 500 (approximately USD 300) for each failure to deliver the annual return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (IR4) for a New Zealand limited company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, due 7 July immediately following the income year; for a non-standard balance date, due within seven months after balance date (tax agents may obtain extensions).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 (approximately USD 150) for the first 30-day period, increasing by NZD 250 per further 30-day period up to NZD 1,000 (approximately USD 600); late payment penalties and use-of-money interest accrue on any unpaid terminal tax at IRD-prescribed rates until the balance is settled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax (GST) returns, including the final GST return for the nominated GST taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due by the 28th day of the month following the end of each GST filing period; where a GST year-end coincides with the company's balance date, the final annual/period return must be filed within one month after that period end. A company making taxable supplies above NZD 60,000 per annum is required to register and file GST.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: GST returns filed late incur a late filing penalty of NZD 250 (approximately USD 150) for companies, plus late payment penalties of 1% per month on overdue GST and use-of-money interest from the due date; persistent non-filing can lead to default GST assessments and enforced collection, although it does not directly affect the company's Companies Register existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholding and director-change notifications embedded in the annual return update process
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors and registered-office changes must be notified to the Companies Office within 10 working days of the change; share transfers must be recorded in the shareholder register without unreasonable delay and reflected on the next annual return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continuing default on statutory register updates is an offence under the Companies Act 1993; the Registrar may decline to accept the subsequent annual return or issue compliance requirements, and repeated non-compliance is taken into account in strike-off removal proceedings for an abandoned company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified audit is statutorily required if the New Zealand limited company is a 'large company' under section 45 of the Companies Act 1993, which exists if any one of the following is exceeded at balance date: (i) consolidated total assets exceed NZD 60,000,000; (ii) consolidated annual revenue exceeds NZD 30,000,000; or (iii) consolidated full-time-equivalent employees number 50 or more. A company is also compulsorily audited if it is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, has made a public offer of equity/debt instruments or is otherwise required by shareholders or the Registrar to have an auditor appointed. No industry-specific audit obligation applies solely because the company operates a PropTech/real-estate SaaS platform with no statutory license requirement. For small companies below these thresholds, an audit may be avoided by passing an audit-exemption shareholder resolution; however, the directors must still ensure financial statements are prepared if required by the shareholders, IRD, or the Companies Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice ('NZ GAAP'). Large for-profit entities must apply NZ equivalents of IFRS (NZ IFRS) with full disclosure. Non-large entities may apply Tier 2 NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR), or Tier 3/4 simplified accounting standards issued by the New Zealand External Reporting Board (XRB) where they qualify. Tax-basis financial statements may be prepared for IRD purposes only and are not a substitute for general-purpose financial statements if audit-legally mandated.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a publicly searchable UBO filing portal; the company must maintain a beneficial ownership register at its registered office and disclose it to the Companies Office or New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit on request. The register must identify each individual who owns or controls more than 25% of the shares or voting rights or who otherwise exercises significant influence over the company. The annual return process serves as the repeated confirmation checkpoint for shareholder details, but every transfer must be entered in the shareholder register promptly once a valid transfer is lodged, the register entries must be updated without unreasonable delay and any resulting change of beneficial ownership must be updated in the beneficial ownership register; a prudent written protocol is the 30-day reconciliation window after each share movement. In addition, directors' details are updated in the Companies Register within 10 working days of any change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: NZD 500 - NZD 2,500 per year (approximately USD 300 - USD 1,500) for a standard New Zealand registered-office and company-secretarial agent service; if the company uses its own registered office at its own business premises, the only compulsory cost is the Companies Office annual return fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: NZD 15,000 - NZD 40,000 per year (approximately USD 9,000 - USD 24,000) for a full statutory audit of a small-to-mid-sized New Zealand SaaS holding/trading company; for an audit-exempt company a review engagement or agreed-upon-procedures engagement typically ranges from NZD 5,000 - NZD 12,000 (approximately USD 3,000 - USD 7,200).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand applies a flat 28% corporate income tax rate. No statutory tax holiday is available; however, a 15% refundable research and development (R&D) tax credit is available for eligible R&D expenditure. Other features include imputation credits and a 5% reduction for qualifying income from transparent foreign entities under certain DTA provisions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (subject to shareholder continuity of 50% or, failing that, the company's business continuity test)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Annual Company Income Tax Return, filed electronically via myIR (mandatory for most entities)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with provisional tax installments and terminal tax due on specific dates)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed no later than 30 September (six months after balance date). Where the company uses a registered tax agent, the deadline is automatically extended to 31 March of the following year for the same balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, IRD number, balance date, and physical address of the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies holding an IRD number must enter the same identifiers; include an address for service in New Zealand and, where applicable, the New Zealand branch address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income from all business activities, including sales, services, interest, dividends, and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies to which New Zealand source income is attributable must declare only income sourced in New Zealand, excluding income derived from a permanent establishment outside New Zealand unless otherwise directed by the IRD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenditure and deductions allowable under the Income Tax Act 2007, such as operating costs, depreciation, interest, salaries, and other ordinary and necessary business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers claim only deductions that are attributable to the New Zealand-source income derived through a permanent establishment. Expenses incurred offshore deemed to support that permanent establishment must be supported by contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income minus allowable deductions, resulting in taxable income or tax loss for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies calculate taxable income exclusively from their New Zealand permanent establishment. Losses may be ring-fenced and carried forward only where the statutory shareholder and business continuity tests are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of income tax at the 28% corporate rate, along with imputation credits and any applicable R&D tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filing entities must apply the 28% rate to the net amount attributable to their New Zealand-source income. DTA relief is not applied as a deduction in Box 5; rather, a treaty reduction is claimed through the withholding tax reconciliation or by requesting a DTA-certified refund via myIR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account (ICA) balance, dividend withholding tax paid, and other credits such as international tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must report imputation credits attached to dividends received and, where applicable, attach imputation credits to own dividend distributions. Foreign tax credits sought under a DTA require attachment of the foreign tax authority assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Related-Party Transactions and Transfer Pricing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border related-party transactions including services, intangibles, loans, and goods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies are required to disclose the aggregate amount of cross-border related-party arrangements and declare that the transfer pricing policies used are arm's length compliant. A local file or master file must be retained if the statutory thresholds are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 triggers a late filing penalty (initial NZ$250 for companies with turnover under NZ$500,000, NZ$500 for larger companies) followed by additional penalties of NZ$200 per month, subject to monthly compounding. In addition, a late payment penalty of 1% of the unpaid tax applies for the first day, then 1% per month thereafter, plus interest on overdue taxes at the IRD prescribed rate (currently 8.07% per annum). Directors who knowingly fail to cause the company to file may be separately assessed for penalties up to NZ$10,000 per shareholder or NZ$5,000 for each instance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) rate on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders is 30%. A reduced rate may be available under an applicable double tax agreement (DTA); a typical DTA rate is 15%, and for certain shareholdings in a New Zealand company the rate may be reduced to 5%. Fully imputed dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder from a New Zealand imputation credit account are exempt from NRWT if the shareholder's country of residence provides for a full credit under the DTA (or if the dividend is treated as fully imputed under New Zealand internal law).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident recipient must provide the New Zealand paying company with a current Certificate of Residence (CoR) issued by the resident tax authority (in English or with an official English translation). The CoR must identify the taxpayer and confirm tax residence for the relevant fiscal year. The paying company is then entitled to withhold at the reduced DTA rate, but must retain the CoR on file together with a completed IRD form (for example IR3NR or a dividend withholding tax reduction certificate) if requested by the IRD. For dividend payments, the recipient must ensure the New Zealand company has applied for a DTA exemption certificate from IRD before payment is made. If the reduced rate is not applied at source, the non-resident must file a New Zealand tax return to claim a refund, attaching the CoR and an explanation of the DTA article relied upon.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory NRWT rate for royalties paid to non-residents is 30%. Under typical DTAs, the royalty withholding rate may be reduced to 10% or 0% in some cases (e.g., on cultural copyright or equipment royalties) when the recipient is the beneficial owner. Interest paid to a non-resident carries a statutory NRWT rate of 30% as well, generally reduced to 10% under most DTAs, and in certain cases to 0% on interest derived by a bank or insurance company. New Zealand also allows the payer to elect to pay the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) at 2% on the gross amount of interest or royalty payments to a non-resident lender or licensor, provided the payer is an approved issuer and the payment does not arise from a fixed establishment of the payer in New Zealand. AIL is a full substitute for NRWT under New Zealand law.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand's transfer pricing rules follow the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines. A New Zealand company that is part of a multinational group with global consolidated revenue of at least NZ$1.1 billion is required to prepare and retain a Master File and a Local File. A Local File alone is required where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions (excluding financing) exceeds NZ$2 million per year, or NZ$500,000 in respect of a related-party financing transaction. Where the annual value of related-party services reaches NZ$1 million, a contemporaneous benchmarking study must be maintained. The IRD may request these documents within 30 days of a formal written request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate statutory Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime similar to captive jurisdictions. However, the Income Tax Act 2007 includes a General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, sections BG 1 and GA 1) that allows the IRD to disregard arrangements lacking commercial substance. Pure holding or shell companies with no employees or physical presence in New Zealand are at a high risk of being recharacterised. Moreover, the capitalisation rules and the New Zealand thin capitalisation rules (interest limitation at 60% debt-to-assets for non-resident owners) impose de facto substance requirements. The IRD will closely scrutinise a cross-border arrangement if the local entity does not maintain board minutes, an identifiable office, banking functions, or administrative personnel that would ordinarily be expected of a substance-based business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating taxable income, overstating deductions, destroying or falsifying records, using shell entities to conceal New Zealand-source profits, or misleading the IRD in relation to cross-border related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under the Crimes Act 1961 and the Tax Administration Act 1994 can result in imprisonment for a term not exceeding 5 years, a fine up to NZ$50,000 for an individual, and for a company penalties up to NZ$100,000 plus recovery of unpaid tax with interest. The IRD may also impose civil shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall for abusive tax positions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in the preparation of false returns may be personally assessed under the anti-avoidance provisions. Personal liability may extend to the full amount of unpaid taxes through the piercing of the corporate veil where the company is merely an instrument. Directors may face a civil restraint order, a travel ban, and, where the evasion scheme involves dishonest activity, imprisonment for up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a New Zealand company that has no physical office, no employees, no operational control, and no meaningful activities other than holding assets or receiving royalties or interest from related parties, while seeking to benefit from New Zealand's DTA network or imputation system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD may disregard the legal form of the entity, aggregate transactions between related parties, and impose additional taxes under the GAAR. Assessment can include penalties of 20% of the shortfall for failing to take reasonable care, increasing to 150% for intentional disregard. The company may also be stripped of its imputation credit balance and be denied deductions for interest or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell entity are exposed to personal liability for the company's unpaid tax and penalties where the company is used to perpetrate a sham or a mere facade. The High Court has the power to make a civil property recovery order against the director's assets up to the value of the tax avoided. The director may also be disqualified from managing companies under the Companies Act 1993 for a period of up to 5 years and be subject to travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Breach (Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: As a PropTech company providing real estate management and rental screening services, the entity may be a reporting entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 if it handles customer funds, facilitates property transactions, or provides financial services to third parties. Non-compliance includes failure to undertake customer due diligence, failure to report suspicious transactions, or failing to maintain the AML/CFT compliance programme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and the supervisor (usually the Department of Internal Affairs for non-bank financial institutions) may impose a civil penalty of up to NZ$4 million for a body corporate for each contravention, and a further penalty of up to NZ$500,000 for each subsequent contravention. A criminal conviction for money laundering can lead to a fine of up to NZ$500,000 and imprisonment for up to 7 years for individuals; senior managers can be imprisoned for up to 2 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers who knew or should have known of the AML/CFT breach may be personally liable for the civil penalty. The FIU may also apply for a director disqualification, freezing orders, and a pecuniary penalty order. A separate offence of knowingly or recklessly providing material assistant to money laundering carries a maximum of 14 years' imprisonment under the Crimes Act 1961.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unpaid Dividend Withholding Tax / Unreported Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a dividend to a non-resident shareholder without deducting NRWT, failing to attach imputation credits, or incorrectly claiming a DTA exemption without the proper CoR on file. Also, making loans or excessive interest payments to related non-residents that exceed the arm's length threshold without appropriate transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is liable for the unpaid NRWT amount plus a penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall (reduced to 20% if the taxpayer makes a voluntary disclosure). If the payer fails to obtain the correct certificate of residence, the full 30% statutory rate applies without reduction, and the payer cannot pass the economic burden to the recipient. Interest accrues daily on the unpaid amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the company's obligation to withhold tax if they were knowingly involved in the payment of a dividend without proper withholding. The director's personal assets may be attached, and the director may be prohibited from leaving New Zealand pending settlement. An order for restitution may be made against the director for the gross amount of the distribution plus interest.
